_comment: GDPR Art. 22 automated decision-making register for the Art. 15 access report. Edit this file directly (via PR) to add, remove, or reword entries — no code change needed. Each entry's `statement` and `safeguards_text` are shown to the reviewer as pre-approved subject-facing text and inserted verbatim into the generated report if selected. Every entry must be validated by the organisation's DPO/legal counsel against what the named system actually does before use — see docs/sar-app.md's 'Automated decision-making' section.

systems.system_name: Risk-based pricing at point of sale (e.g. insurance premiums, retail personalised pricing)
systems.human_review_exists: None — the price is calculated and offered without human review.
systems.statement: We use automated processing to calculate the price you are offered, taking into account factors such as your history with us, the product or cover selected, and risk or value characteristics associated with you. This directly determines the price you are offered.
systems.safeguards_text: You have the right to request a manual review of this pricing decision, to express your view on the factors used, and to contest the outcome.

systems.system_name: Ongoing behaviour/usage-based dynamic pricing (e.g. telematics insurance, usage-based retail or subscription pricing)
systems.human_review_exists: None for routine adjustments — a person can review on request.
systems.statement: Where you participate in a usage-based programme, automated processing analyses your behaviour or usage patterns — such as driving behaviour, purchase frequency, or activity levels — to adjust your price on an ongoing basis. This can increase or decrease the price you pay.
systems.safeguards_text: You have the right to query a specific pricing adjustment, request the underlying scoring factors be reviewed by a person, and opt out of the programme in favour of standard pricing.

systems.system_name: Automated eligibility/risk decisioning (e.g. insurance underwriting, credit or account approval)
systems.human_review_exists: A human reviewer checks every declined or referred outcome before it is finalised; accepted outcomes are not individually reviewed.
systems.statement: Automated processing assesses risk factors from your application to produce a recommended eligibility outcome (accept, decline, or refer for further review). A human reviewer checks every declined or referred outcome before it is finalised; accepted outcomes are not individually reviewed.
systems.safeguards_text: You have the right to request human review of a decline or referral, to provide additional context, and to contest the outcome.

systems.system_name: Fraud detection & triage (e.g. insurance claims, banking transactions, retail orders/returns)
systems.human_review_exists: A specialist investigator reviews before any adverse decision is made — confirm this holds for every case before using this entry.
systems.statement: When you submit a claim, make a transaction, or place an order, automated processing scores it against known fraud indicators to prioritise investigation. A high score routes it to a specialist investigator for human review before any decision is made; it does not by itself determine the outcome.
systems.safeguards_text: Since a person reviews before any adverse decision, Art. 22 does not strictly apply — confirm this is factually true for every case before using this framing.

systems.system_name: Automated settlement/payout processing (e.g. insurance claims, retail refunds)
systems.human_review_exists: None for cases within the automated criteria — a handler reviews everything outside them.
systems.statement: Straightforward claims or refund requests below £500 and meeting defined criteria are settled automatically without individual human review, using processing that checks cover/eligibility, value, and supporting evidence against our rules. Cases outside these criteria are reviewed by a handler.
systems.safeguards_text: You have the right to request the automated settlement be reviewed by a handler, to express your view, and to contest the outcome.

systems.system_name: Ongoing relationship risk/value scoring (e.g. insurance renewal pricing, credit limit review, loyalty tier recalculation)
systems.human_review_exists: None — a person can review on request.
systems.statement: Periodically, automated processing recalculates your risk or value profile using updated account and history data to determine terms such as your renewal price, credit limit, or tier. This can result in different terms than your previous period.
systems.safeguards_text: You have the right to request a manual review of the recalculated terms and to contest the underlying risk or value profile.

systems.system_name: Affordability/creditworthiness check (e.g. insurance premium finance, retail buy-now-pay-later, banking credit)
systems.human_review_exists: None — a person can review on request.
systems.statement: If you choose to pay by instalments or apply for credit, automated processing assesses affordability using information such as payment history to decide whether terms can be offered, and on what terms. This can affect whether credit or instalments are available to you and the terms offered.
systems.safeguards_text: You have the right to request human review of an affordability decision and to contest the outcome.

systems.system_name: Automated identity/KYC verification decisioning (e.g. account opening, age verification, transaction checks)
systems.human_review_exists: A human reviewer checks every failed verification before you are refused service — confirm this holds for every case before using this entry.
systems.statement: When you open an account, verify your identity, or complete certain transactions, automated processing checks the information and documents you provide against identity and verification data sources to produce a pass or fail outcome. A failed check is referred to a human reviewer before you are refused service; it does not by itself finalise a refusal.
systems.safeguards_text: Since a person reviews before any refusal, Art. 22 does not strictly apply — confirm this is factually true for every case before using this framing. You may request the verification factors be explained.

systems.system_name: Account suspension/restriction for suspicious activity (e.g. banking fraud holds, marketplace seller suspension, policy restriction)
systems.human_review_exists: None at the point of suspension — a person reviews before the suspension is lifted or made permanent.
systems.statement: Automated processing monitors account activity against known risk indicators and can automatically suspend or restrict your account when activity matches those indicators, to prevent suspected fraud or misuse while the matter is investigated. This can immediately affect your ability to use the account or service.
systems.safeguards_text: You have the right to request human review of a suspension, to provide an explanation, and to have the suspension lifted if it is not upheld.

systems.human_review_exists: None for claims within standard thresholds — a person reviews disputed or edge-case claims.
systems.statement: When your journey is delayed, automated processing calculates your compensation entitlement using your journey data — including scheduled and actual arrival times — against our Delay Repay policy. This determines whether you receive compensation and how much.
systems.safeguards_text: You have the right to request a manual review of a compensation decision, to query the journey data used, and to contest the outcome.

systems.human_review_exists: A revenue protection officer reviews before any penalty fare is issued — confirm this holds for every case before using this entry.
systems.statement: Automated processing analyses tap-in/tap-out data to flag journeys with irregular or missing fare payment. A flagged journey is reviewed by a revenue protection officer before any penalty fare or enforcement action is taken; it does not by itself determine the outcome.
systems.safeguards_text: Since a person reviews before any adverse decision, Art. 22 does not strictly apply — confirm this is factually true for every case before using this framing. You may request the flagging factors be explained.

systems.human_review_exists: None — this determines communications only, not an entitlement or service outcome.
systems.statement: Automated processing matches your recorded travel patterns against live service disruption data to decide whether to send you a disruption alert for a given line or station. This affects which notifications you receive, not any entitlement or charge.
systems.safeguards_text: You can opt out of disruption notifications at any time in your account preferences.
